1.why: The UI uses a clean sans-serif typeface with comfortable line height throughout (e.g., the body text on the verify-identity screen), though letter spacing is default rather than notably generous.

2.why: No italics or all-caps text appears in any heading, button, or instruction, and all guidance is presented in short light paragraphs rather than dense blocks.

3.why: Content sits in a narrow single-column card with full-width buttons and large text that should map cleanly onto a phone viewport, although only desktop-width screenshots were provided.

4.why: Instructions are one to three short plain-language sentences per screen, such as 'Enter the six-digit identity code.'

5.why: Most inputs show format examples via placeholders ('ABCD-1234-EF56-7890', '6 digits', 'marcus@example.com'), though the identity-code field itself has an empty placeholder.

6.why: The user is forced to scan the ever-growing dense monospace Logs panel to obtain every test code, which by the regeneration step is a long block of text that must be read to proceed.

7.why: No copy-to-clipboard affordance is provided for the 26-character secret or the recovery codes, and the flow explicitly demands manual transcription via the 'Manual secret entry' field.

8.why: Although the text mentions 'scanning a code,' no QR code or scannable equivalent is rendered anywhere on the provisioning screen, only the plain-text secret and account label.

9.why: The code fields are plain text inputs with no visible one-time-code autofill affordance, and nothing on any screen indicates password-manager support.

10.why: Each screen pairs a bold heading with a prominent full-width blue primary button, though the settings page stacks four full-width buttons which slightly dilutes the emphasis.

11.why: Each screen requests a single submission at a time, and the settings page offers mutually exclusive navigation choices rather than simultaneous tasks.

12.why: Plain status lines follow each action ('Authenticator verification succeeded.', 'Challenge ready. Enter the test code from Logs.'), though some messages state what happened without saying what comes next.

13.why: The failed verification in the last screenshots remains retryable, 'Start over' and the challenge/regeneration buttons stay available, and no lockout or penalty is shown.

14.why: The only observed error, 'The request could not be completed.', neither identifies the problem nor explains how to fix it, even though it avoids blaming language.

15.why: No countdown, expiry indicator, or session timeout appears on any screen, so reading is untimed and code entry is not visibly rushed beyond inherent TOTP rotation.
